verdict.rationale: Solid ships first-party state management in the core framework: Stores and Context handle global state without a third-party library, alongside signals for reactive and derived state. A community user corroborates the simple, deep store-based state handling. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the Store API (nested updates, patterns) in the evidence, and confirmation of mature state devtools (a community report calls dev tools alpha).

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official first-party state management library maintained alongside the framework

citations.quote: Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores: you don't have to reach for a third party library to manage global state
Declare your state and use it throughout your app, and when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.
Create a piece of reactive state, giving us an accessor, count(), and a setter, setCount()
